best_plan.name: p6
best_plan.rationale: p6 achieved the best observed result: perfect quality (f1_score 1.0) while still keeping execution cost very low at about $0.0043. It first uses an exact filter on idx to shrink the review set, then applies two targeted semantic sentiment filters, joins positive and negative reviews, removes accidental self-pairs with an exact post-join filter, and finally projects the required output fields. Compared with p4, p6 costs only slightly more but improves quality from 0.5 to 1.0, which is the best cost-quality trade-off observed.

cost_model_explanation: The cost model helped compare variants before execution and showed that the expensive part was always the LLM-based sentiment filtering and join, not the exact filter/project steps. That pushed the design toward filtering by idx first, projecting only needed fields before the join, and using the cheaper GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE model rather than larger models. Even though absolute estimates were high, they were still useful for ranking plans and steering toward low-cost semantic operators.
